intended_object: The constructor of an idele of K from local coordinates: units z_w ∈ K_w^× at the infinite places and units z_v ∈ K_v^× at the finite places, integral units (in O_v^×) for almost all v. It realises the inverse of the classical identification I_K ≅ ∏_w K_w^× × ∏'_v (K_v^×, O_v^×). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: Mathlib's IdeleGroup R K is 𝔸[R,K]ˣ, the units of (∏_w K_w) × (finite adele ring). The body sends zi through MulEquiv.piUnits.symm to a unit of the infinite adele ring. It sends z through RestrictedProduct.mkUnit, using hz (z_v ∈ O_v^× cofinitely often), to a unit of the finite adele ring. MulEquiv.prodUnits.symm then combines the two into a unit of the product. This is exactly the idele with the given coordinates, and the library proves that both coordinates are recovered and that the construction agrees with the inverse of its localUnitsEquiv. The setting (a Dedekind domain R with fraction field K) is the same as Mathlib's IdeleGroup, so the definition is not too narrow. Mathlib has no ready-made constructor for whole ideles; RestrictedProduct.mkUnit covers only the finite part.
